I, JUSTICE RICHARD LUSSICK, PRESIDENT OF THE RESIDUAL SPECIAL
COURT FOR SIERRA LEONE, (“Residual Special Court”, “RSCSL” or “Court”);
RECALLING the Decision of the President on Application for Conditional Early Release
dated 8 September 2020, granting Augustine Gbao conditional early release pursuant to
Article 24 of the Statute of the Residual Special Court for Sierra Leone as annexed to the
Agreement Between the United Nations and the Government of Sierra Leone on the
Establishment of the Residual Special Court for Sierra Leone signed on 11 August 2010
(Statute), Rule 124 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Residual Special Court
for Sierra Leone (Rules) and Article 8 of the Practice Direction on Conditional Early
Release of Persons Convicted by the Special Court for Sierra Leone (Practice Direction);
RECALLING that Augustine Gbao was granted early release subject to certain strict
conditions and further special conditions including that set out in paragraph 83
subparagraph (viii) of the Decision which reads: [t]he applicant must commit to producing
a community volunteer service plan in support of his stated commitment to contribute to
restitution of victims for [the President’s approval] within 90 days of release; and that
Augustine Gbao’s community volunteer service plan was approved by the President in June
2021 with a requirement for him to give written updates on all activities undertaken to the
Court every three (3) months, the first of such updates being due on 30 September 2021;
NOTING the interoffice memorandum dated 11 March 2025, addressed to the President
from the Principal Defender by way of update on Augustine Gbao’s compliance with his
conditional early release obligations including the special condition contained in paragraph
83 subparagraph (viii) of the Decision, in which the Principal Defender stated inter alia
that: “[t]hat Mr. Gbao’s current health situation deprives him of the ability to effectively
engage in agricultural activities in his gardens which, in effect, limits his compliance with
his modified obligations as directed by the President in his Decision of the 27th January
2023”;
2
Prosecutor v Augustine Gbao
RSCSL-04-15-ES 21 July 2025

5894
HAVING RECEIVED a letter transmitted by the Principal Defender on behalf of
Augustine Gbao, in which Augustine Gbao is seeking a further review of the Special
Condition in paragraph 83 subparagraph (viii) of the Decision stating that he has “not been
able to actively engage in any hard work including agricultural activities” due to his present
health condition and appeals “for a review of the agricultural activities” (Request);
CONSEQUENTLY DIRECTING on 27 March 2025, that (a) the Registrar is to submit
an independent and comprehensive medical examination report on the health of Augustine
Gbao no later than 30 April 2025, such report to include expert medical opinion as to the
extent of any limitations on his physical activity due to his medical condition; and (b) the
Principal Defender is to submit an alternative proposal for community service by
Augustine Gbao, no later than 30 April 2025;
HAVING RECEIVED a confidential medical opinion and medical examination reports
from the Registrar, pursuant to my Directive for submission of an independent and
comprehensive medical report on the health of Augustine Gbao;
NOTING that the general conclusion from the interpretation of medical records and
medical opinion received is that despite Augustine Gbao´s health condition, he is
physically and mentally fit to engage in any medium to small scale livelihood activities;
NOTING that the further alternative proposal is requesting the President to review the
special condition in paragraph 83 subparagraph (viii) of the Decision as follows:
“…having regard to his health which has deteriorated, that the President permits him to
engage in community sensitisation on peace building and peace consolidation through
radio discussion programmes. He further proposes that he is willing to undertake such a
programme once every three months, subject to the President’s approval”;
HAVING REQUESTED and RECEIVED the views of the Prosecutor and the
Monitoring Authority (the Sierra Leone Police) on the request pursuant to Clause 11(B) of
the Practice Direction, and the views of the Registrar pursuant to Rule 33(B) of the Rules;
3
Prosecutor v Augustine Gbao
RSCSL-04-15-ES 21 July 2025

5895
NOTING that the Prosecutor submits that having reviewed Augustine Gbao’s current
medical report, he sees no material change in his physical condition as it was two years ago
that led to the January 2023 modification of his Conditional Early Release Agreement and
that Augustine Gbao has provided insufficient justification that the proposed change will
serve as a suitable alternative to his current reduced Conditional Early Release obligation;
further submits that if the President is considering to grant the Request, Augustine Gbao’s
alternate proposal should go beyond mere headline-catching and provide concrete details
of how his proposed “once every three months” radio discussion programme will benefit
his Blama community, and Sierra Leone as a whole; and that the current proposal does not
discuss the structure or content of the programme, the intended audience, nor provide an
indication whether other persons, and if so who, will be involved in these radio
presentations;
NOTING the Registrar’s submission that: being conversant with the facts and
developments pertaining to Augustine Gbao’s compliance with the conditions of his early
release and the expert medical opinion submitted on his health, she does not object to
Augustine Gbao’s alternative proposal of engaging in community sensitisation on
peacebuilding and peace consolidation through radio discussion programmes, because it
supports the Court’s outreach, peacebuilding and accountability efforts; proposes that
should the President approve Augustine Gbao’s alternative proposal, the proposed radio
discussion programmes should be held twice every three months, instead of once, because
increasing the frequency of such programmes would enhance the impact of the Court’s
outreach efforts and provide more consistent engagement with Sierra Leoneans; proposes
that the Registrar’s office will liaise with the Defence office to plan its implementation
since it aligns with the community outreach programmes within the remit of the RSCSL
Registry;
NOTING that the Sierra Leone Police (the Monitoring Authority) has no objection to the
approval of the Request based on Augustine Gbao’s medical situation as according to
4
Prosecutor v Augustine Gbao
RSCSL-04-15-ES 21 July 2025

5896
reports in their possession, Augustine Gbao has otherwise consistently complied with the
terms of his conditional early release;
RECALLING that pursuant to Clause 11(B) of the Practice Direction: “[t]he President
may from time to time, review the conditions of the Conditional Early Release Agreement,
propio motu, or upon the request of the Convicted Person, the Monitoring Authority or the
Prosecutor. In the absence of a finding pursuant to Clause 12 that the Convicted Person has
violated a condition, the President may modify a condition of the agreement only with the
consent of the Convicted Person, and after consideration of the views of the Prosecutor and
the Monitoring Authority”;
HAVING CONSIDERED the entirety of the submissions before me including Augustine
Gbao’s medical report which states that he is physically and mentally fit to involve in any
medium to small scale livelihood activities, but highlights serious medical conditions that
Augustine Gbao suffers from and advises that he does medical checkups every three
months to prevent a further deterioration, thereby warranting serious considerations about
his health in the future; the concerns raised by the Prosecutor as well as the Registrar’s and
Monitoring Authority’s submissions;
CONSIDERING that Augustine Gbao’s alternative proposal/volunteer service plan of
engaging in community sensitisation on peacebuilding and peace consolidation through
radio discussion programmes, may support the Court’s outreach, peacebuilding and
accountability efforts and that such programmes would enhance the impact of the Court’s
outreach efforts, provide more consistent engagement with his community in Blama and
Sierra Leoneans in general;
PURSUANT to Clause 11(B) of the Practice Direction;
GRANT Augustine Gbao’s further request for review of the Conditional Early Release
Agreement and the Special Condition in paragraph 83 subparagraph (viii) of the Decision,
and
5
Prosecutor v Augustine Gbao
RSCSL-04-15-ES 21 July 2025

5897
DIRECT that the Special Condition shall constitute the following:
(i) As part of his community volunteer service plan, Augustine Gbao shall
participate in radio discussion programmes on peacebuilding and peace
consolidation which are to be held twice every three months;
(ii) . The radio programmes shall be broadcast in Slama and in other parts of Sierra
Leone;
(iii) The Registrar 's Office shall liaise with the Defence office to discuss the
structure and content of the programmes, plan their implementation and align
them with the community outreach programmes within the remit ofthe RSCSL
Registry;
(iv) Augustine Gbao shall submit the content of the programmes developed to the
President for approval within 21 days of publication of this Decision.
FURTHER ORDER that Augustine Gbao must comply strictly with the terms of the
reviewed special condition of early release, including the existing requirement to submit
comprehensive quarterly written updates on activities undertaken therein to the President.
ALL other conditions of early release imposed in the Decision, remain the same.
Done at The Hague, The Netherlands
This 2151 day of July 2025
Prosecutor v Augustine Gbao
RSCSL-04-/5-ES 21 July 2025
